feed.title: The PLA Watch
feed.subtitle: Weekly signals from Chinese military media — a publication of China Mil Watch

entry.title: The PLA Watch: A Partner Navy East of Taiwan
entry.summary: Chinese official media spent the week presenting the PLA to audiences outside it. A bilateral passage exercise with Indonesia was placed in waters east of Taiwan, a Chinese diplomat contested Washington's account of a missile test in Geneva, and two accounts of women in combat aviation carried the same institutional message.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Scarborough Shoal, Platform Disclosures, and the Limits of Anniversary Week
entry.summary: The PLA's 99th founding anniversary produced a cluster of capability disclosures and a coordinated exercise response to Philippine legal moves at Huangyan Island, but reading them together requires separating deliberate messaging from institutional routine.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Army Day, Scarborough Shoal, and a Week of Deliberate Disclosure
entry.summary: The PLA's 99th founding anniversary was used to advance multiple simultaneous messaging lines: a named joint naval-air exercise at Scarborough Shoal timed to the Philippines' baseline declaration, first footage of the Type 076's electromagnetic catapult, and a model-soldier roster that incidentally confirmed the Military Space Force's internal structure.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Joint Sea-2026, the Y-20B Abroad, and the Week's Quieter Signals
entry.summary: China-Russia naval exercises concluded with a live-fire Pacific patrol component and fresh subsurface integration; separately, PLA Daily confirmed the Y-20B's first international flight and its regiment's combat patrol record across three maritime theaters.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Beijing's Public SLBM Test and What It Was Designed to Do
entry.summary: China's announced submarine-launched ballistic missile test mattered because Beijing chose to describe it in unusual detail. The rest of the week showed familiar patterns in disaster relief, China-Russia naval cooperation, and far-seas operations.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Scarborough Shoal, July 1st Loyalty, and What Routine Looks Like
entry.summary: Southern Theater Command described a month of joint naval and air activity around Huangyan Island as combat readiness patrols. The rest of the week showed how the PLA turns Party anniversaries into institutional instruction.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Carriers, Drones, and the Rocket Force's Manning Problem
entry.summary: A far-sea exercise paired Liaoning with an amphibious assault ship formation. Two quieter reports, on reduced-manning missile operations and a PLA-wide drone contest, showed where the force still sees friction beneath its modernization drive.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: The CCG Statement That Stood Apart
entry.summary: One MND spokesperson statement tied CCG operations east of Taiwan to cross-strait nationalist obligation and Japan-Philippines maritime talks. The rest of the week was dense with political work, useful less for drama than for what it documents about institutional friction.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Combat Realism, Institutional Friction, and One Confirmation Worth Noting
entry.summary: A week dominated by training reform narratives and political work — with one MND press briefing that cut through the noise by putting the Liaoning carrier strike group officially on the map.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Loitering Munitions, Rocket Force Readiness, and the Coast Guard's Expanding Remit
entry.summary: This week’s PLA Daily signal sat below the headline layer, where a doctrinal article on low-cost loitering munitions and a granular Rocket Force training feature converged with a CCG patrol east of Taiwan tied to Japan-Philippines maritime talks.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Senior Cadre Oversight, Electronic Warfare, and the Week's Institutional Texture
entry.summary: The CMC issued a formal 26-article directive on managing its senior officer corps. The Southern Theater Command publicly acknowledged jamming a NATO warship. The rest of the week was mostly institutional maintenance — but that maintenance is worth reading carefully.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Institutional Friction and the Gap Between Form and Function
entry.summary: A full week of PLA Daily coverage with no flagged significant articles — but internal-reform coverage offers a useful baseline for the implementation gaps the institution is still naming publicly.

entry.title: Fujian’s Air Wing Takes Shape as the Rocket Force Trains for Failure
entry.summary: KJ-600 carrier qualification confirmed aboard Fujian. A Rocket Force unit publishes the failure that prompted its crew-hardening model. 85 articles, May 10–16, 2026.

entry.title: The PLA Watch: Two Defense Ministers, One Verdict
entry.summary: Pilot edition based on three days of observed data (7–9 May 2026), not a full weekly readout. Across 42 articles from PLA Daily and affiliated outlets, the suspended death sentences against Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu — two consecutive former defense ministers — stand apart from otherwise routine coverage.
